title.narrative: Australia Assists - Global Humanitarian Specialists Deployment Program (2024 -2029)

description.narrative: Australia Assists (2024-29) builds on the success of the previous phase of the program (2017-2014) and continues to support global deployment of civilian humanitarian specialists to work with global governments, multilateral agencies and communities to prepare for and respond to disasters and the effects of conflict. The program responds to sudden onset and emerging humanitarian needs as they arise, with a focus on the Pacific, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa regions. The Program is committed to cross-cutting themes such as localisation, Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), and climate resilience.

description.narrative: During planned resurfacing works to Nauru’s only airport runway, the Government of Nauru—supported by the Government of Australia—identified 96 metallurgical anomalies beneath the runway surface, indicating the presence of possible unexploded ordnance (UXO). To safely investigate and remove any confirmed UXOs, airport operations needed to be suspended, raising concerns about humanitarian access and national supply chains. Through Australia Assists, a Humanitarian Risk Planner was deployed to support the Government of Nauru’s National Emergency Services (NES) manage this scenario. ‍ This deployment led analysis of medium-term impacts of an airport closure, short-term contingency planning and medium-term preparedness measures. Coordination support was provided for the investigation of the anomalies, 3 of which were confirmed to be UXOs. Household surveys were conducted, evacuation zones and shelters established, and communication systems and management plans for vulnerable households implemented, strengthening inclusion. New linkages were established between stakeholders identifying the opportunity for joint mitigation strategies. The maximum airport closure time was reduced from 14 to 3 days, and over three instances, NES successfully evacuated more than 2,400 people, enabling safe clearance of the UXOs. Facilitation of training scenarios and development of standard operating procedures left NES staff better equipped for future emergencies and disasters.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Jordan faces significant climate challenges, including water scarcity, increasing temperatures, and land degradation. These challenges necessitate urgent action to develop and implement adaptive strategies that strengthen resilience and support sustainable development, particularly in rural communities. Through Australia Assists, a Climate Change Specialist was deployed to the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to support national and regional stakeholders with capacity building, policy advice, and implementation of practical climate-smart solutions. ‍ The deployment informed the ELEVATE 2025 Fund project, resulting in an anticipated 15% reduction in project costs. Workshops were delivered and capability built among stakeholders to adopt climate-smart solutions and implement adaptive measures to diversify rural incomes. Low-emission, climate-resilient practices were integrated into agricultural value chains. Innovative climate mitigation approaches, such as data sharing agreements and joint early warning systems, were implemented improving timeliness and accuracy of interventions. Climate change adaptation and disaster resilience were improved, and capacity for prevention, mitigation, and early action were enhanced. Strengthened multi-sector partnerships will enable rapid mobilization of resources and expertise during crises. A USD100M funding proposal was developed seeking support from international climate financing institutions support for further projects to address critical climate resilience gaps in Jordan's agricultural sector.

One of the largest Rohingya refugee camps in the world is in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh. Among this marginalised population is an often-overlooked group – people living with a disability. Australia Assists deployed a Disability Inclusion Officer to UNHCR to support work to increase the visibility of people with a disability in Cox’s Bazar. ‍ The deployment focused on representative data collection, capacity and awareness-building, and local participation, and aligning in-camp disability data collection processes with international standardized tools. Training was delivered to UNHCR and implementing partners’ staff in disability awareness and data collection, and community consultations were led with people living with a disability. Good practices were embedded and the relationship with local partner, Handicap International, strengthened. Specific outcomes included an increase disability prevalence data in Cox’s Bazaar from 0.8% to 3.05%; weekly disability awareness training conducted for over 1,500 UNHCR and implementing partner staff, building inclusive capacity; and specialised training delivered to 28 chosen ‘Disability Inclusion Champions’. The deployment also mobilised local participation: 1,251 people with a disability and caregivers (59% male, 41% female) from across 33 camps engaged in ‘self-help groups’ to inform disability service provision and programming.

The Eastern Mediterranean region was grappling with a widespread cholera outbreak, exacerbated by escalating armed conflict and the growing impacts of climate change. In response, a Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Specialist was deployed through Australia Assists to the WHO Regional Hub in Amman, Jordan, to support coordinated regional response efforts across 9 affected countries. ‍ The deployment focused on strengthening WASH systems and interventions to help save lives, prevent the spread of disease, and alleviate human suffering. Activities included contributions by the WASH Specialist to the Regional Eastern Mediterranean Cholera Preparedness and Response Strategic Plan in EMR (2025- 28); support to 9 country offices to implement the ‘WASH Facility Improvement Tool’ (WASH FIT), which focused on improvement of WASH conditions within healthcare facilities; and preparation of Chlorination guidelines for drinking water disinfection in Health Facilities. The deployment resulted in strengthened regional architecture through formation of a regional strategy to be contextualised and adapted by national agencies and partners to incorporate WASH into the planning and prevention of Cholera outbreak management; and the upskilling of 9 national agencies to integrate regional systems and tools that will strengthen WASH conditions in healthcare facilities support the prevention of Cholera outbreaks.
